definition.name: NXsynchronization

symbol.name: nE
symbol.doc: Number of recorded events (laser shots, pump pulses or pump-probe pairs). Every per-event array in this group has this length and the order of the event list of the entry it belongs to.

definition.doc:
How two or more pulsed beams are held in a known time relation, and how well that relation held while data were taken.
Pump-probe experiments set the delay between a pump and a probe pulse. The delay itself is recorded where NeXus already puts it, ``NXbeam/pulse_delay`` (readback) and ``NXbeam/pulse_delay_set`` (target), on the probe beam, with ``@reference_beam`` pointing to the pump beam. This group records what the delay is measured against and what makes it valid: the synchronization scheme, the reference clock, the lock state per event, the jitter, the mechanism that sets the delay, and the calibration of time zero.
A delay value is only meaningful together with the time zero it was calibrated against. Writers should therefore store the delay device's own coordinate (for example an ``NXpositioner`` for an optical delay line) and derive ``pulse_delay`` from it and ``time_zero``. When time zero is recalibrated, ``pulse_delay`` can be rewritten, keeping the earlier values as a variant (see the NeXus rule on variants).

field.name: scheme
field.doc:
How the time relation between the beams is established.
* ``common oscillator``: pump and probe are derived from one laser, for example by splitting the beam; the delay is a difference in path length. * ``rf locked``: a laser oscillator is phase-locked to the radio-frequency master clock of an accelerator or storage ring. * ``trigger only``: the sources are triggered from a common timing system without phase locking; the jitter is set by the trigger electronics. * ``measured per event``: the relation is not controlled tightly enough, and the arrival time of each event is measured instead (see ``arrival_time_correction``).

field.name: reference
field.doc: Name of the reference the timing is held against, for example "PETRA III RF master clock" or "DRACO front-end oscillator".

field.name: reference_frequency
field.doc: Frequency of the reference, for example 499.6655 MHz for the PETRA III master clock.

field.name: frequency_ratio
field.doc: Ratio of the locked frequency to ``reference_frequency``, for example 1/6 when the laser oscillator is locked to the sixth subharmonic.

field.name: locked
field.doc: Whether the synchronization was locked. A scalar when it held for the whole entry; an array of length nE when it is known per event. An event recorded while unlocked has no valid delay.

field.name: timing_jitter
field.doc: Root-mean-square timing jitter between the pump and the probe at the interaction point, as characterized. A scalar for a characterization, or an array of length nE when it is measured per event.

attribute.name: method
attribute.doc: How the jitter was determined, for example "phase-noise measurement of the PLL" or "spread of a cross-correlation".

field.name: delay_mechanism
field.doc: What sets the delay. More than one value when coarse and fine settings are combined (for example ``bunch selection`` for steps of one bunch spacing and ``electronic phase shift`` within one spacing).

field.name: delay_range
field.doc: Smallest and largest delay the mechanism can set.

field.name: delay_resolution
field.doc: Smallest delay step the mechanism can set.

field.name: time_zero
field.doc: The delay-device setting at which pump and probe coincide at the interaction point, in the device's time coordinate. ``pulse_delay`` is the device readback minus this value.

attribute.name: method
attribute.doc: How time zero was found, for example "cross-correlation in a nonlinear crystal", "onset of the Debye-Waller intensity drop in Bi", or "onset of transient reflectivity".

attribute.name: determined_at
attribute.doc: When this time-zero calibration was made.

field.name: arrival_time_correction
field.doc: Per-event correction to the delay from an arrival-time measurement (a timing tool, a bunch arrival monitor or a pulse arrival monitor). The corrected delay of event i is the readback delay plus this value.

attribute.name: source
attribute.doc: Path to the group that holds the arrival-time measurement.

group.doc: Details of a phase-locked loop used for ``rf locked`` synchronization. NXphase_lock_loop is a contributed definition written for AFM; its reference frequency, phase error and hardware fields apply unchanged.
Hardware of the synchronization and delay chain, for example the PLL electronics or a direct digital synthesizer used as phase shifter.
The delay device in its own coordinate, for example the position of an optical delay line or the phase setting of a phase shifter.
Readbacks sampled independently of the events, for example the lock state or the PLL phase error over time.
